readme.text:
How to read this file

• Rows = personas: Student (phone, no login), Faculty, Management.
• M1–M3 are ONE working prototype — press Play on M1 and tap through.
• Every name, course and number is SAMPLE DATA for design only. It is NOT test evidence: Chapter 7–8 data must come from a real class session.
• Mood scale is diverging (orange = struggling, grey = neutral, blue = with it) and is always text-labelled, so it never relies on colour alone.

tA.text: Student · scan desk QR, one tap, done

nM1.text: Context is pre-filled from the QR + timetable (room, course, slot), so the student's only job is one tap. Faces are custom SVG, not OS emoji: identical on every phone and no device-specific rendering to fingerprint.

nM2.text: Pace is optional and separate from mood: 'confused because too fast' and 'confused because unclear' need different fixes from the faculty. Send stays one thumb-reach away.

nM3.text: States exactly what is stored and what isn't. Trust is the product: if students suspect tracking, participation and honesty both collapse.

nM4.text: Anti-spam: one tap per device per 10 minutes, via a random daily device code. This is the ASSUMED answer to PROJECT.md decision #3 — confirm before building. It does NOT stop someone outside the room with a photo of the QR.

nM5.text: Outside a scheduled slot, input is closed and the next lecture is shown. Stops off-hours noise from polluting a lecture's data.

nF1.text: College email sign-in; role (faculty / coordinator / HOD) decides the landing page. Students never sign in anywhere.

nF2.text: Today view answers 'how is my class going right now?' in one glance. 'Open a quick check' is the PRD's periodic prompt, triggered by faculty rather than a fixed hourly timer.

nF3.text: The money screen. Topic markers turn a mood chart into a teaching insight: confusion spiked 7 min into Apriori and recovered after the worked example. Buckets with fewer than 5 taps are hidden to protect anonymity.

nF4.text: Trends, not single data points (PRD risk: misreading one-offs). The heatmap shows WHERE in the hour confusion recurs across weeks.

nA1.text: Deliberately shows slots and rooms, never a faculty leaderboard. If it becomes a ranking tool, faculty stop opening quick checks and the data dies. Flag this as a design decision in the report.

nA2.text: Regenerating a QR invalidates the old one — the fix when a photo of a desk QR leaks to a WhatsApp group.

nA3.text: Timetable mapping is what makes anonymous taps analytically useful: room + time → course + faculty. CSV import keeps it maintainable (PRD assumption: schedule stays current).

nA4.text: A6 desk card, laminated. Promise of anonymity printed right next to the QR.
